aspect: EXAMPLE - the totals, with their disagreements
description: The RNPDNO recorded roughly 367,392 disappearances since 1952 as of July 2025, of whom 237,382 were located and 130,010 remain missing. A March 2026 government update cited 394,645 records, with 262,111 located - 240,211 alive and 21,900 dead. La Jornada reported 132,534 disappeared, most from the last twenty years.
energy_note: Somewhere above a hundred and thirty thousand.

description: The IACHR reported that of 128,713 people registered as disappeared as of 3 June 2025, 76.83% were men. Red Lupa found the split stable between May 2022 and May 2025. State variation is wide - Sinaloa 92%, Jalisco 86%.
energy_note: Three quarters of the missing are men.

description: Men aged 20-34 and women aged 19-24 are the most frequently disappeared groups; people aged 20-34 accounted for at least 30,548 cases, about 40% of the total in one cut of the data. Recent reporting indicates the average age is falling, with 15-19 year olds now leading.
energy_note: Twenty to thirty-four, and getting younger.

description: The official count is 'depurada' - cleaned - and it is estimated that for every reported disappearance there are at least 1.5 never brought to prosecutors, largely from fear of reprisals. One source reports the 2025 sex split shifting to 62.84% men, against the historic 76-77%. The number is a political object as well as a statistic.
energy_note: The count is itself disputed, annually.

description: Jalisco, Estado de México, Tamaulipas, Veracruz and Nuevo León account for 44.3% of cases; Jalisco alone had 15,330. Active cases of young men concentrate in Jalisco, Estado de México and Chihuahua.
energy_note: Five states hold nearly half of it.

description: Without a body there is no funeral, no inheritance, no remarriage and no end to searching. The family is suspended indefinitely in a state with no social script for it.
energy_note: No funeral, no death certificate, no permission to stop.

aspect: Declaring him dead is required to get anything and feels like betrayal
description: Accessing accounts, property or benefits requires a declaration of absence or death, so the administrative system forces the family to give up before they are ready.
energy_note: Asked to sign that her son is dead, to pay his mortgage.
